long_biography.plain_text:
At Tjuvholmen, Olav H. Selvaag helped turn an Oslo waterfront into a mixed-use district centred on the Astrup Fearnley Museum and public sculpture. The project became a defining expression of his preference for shaping neighbourhoods around cultural or recreational destinations.

Selvaag brought an MSc from Stanford University, property-management work at KLP Eiendom and US executive experience to the family group, taking posts at Selvaagbygg and Selvaag Pluss from 1998. He later pursued the SNØ indoor ski arena at Lørenskog for a decade despite internal scepticism and difficult financing. The arena opened as the anchor for a planned district of homes, workplaces and leisure uses.
